Now we're building the delivery of (almost) everything and you'll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe. Working at Wolt isn't always easy, but it's definitely exciting. Here you'll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You'll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you're a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life. We're looking for a Product Manager to own our search experience that millions of customers land on when they open DoorDash, Wolt, or Deliveroo, and the single biggest lever we have on what they find. The role sits in our Core Consumer organisation in the Search domain, which is responsible for the in-app experience. You'll be building on a global stack, and your roadmap will be a mix: global platform problems that apply worldwide, global capabilities we're accelerating into EMEA markets, and EMEA-specific problems worth solving properly rather than working around. Search is where customers tell us exactly what they want. Getting it right across restaurants, grocery, and retail - in every language we operate in - is one of the highest-intent and hardest problems in the app. What you'll work on Query understanding, Autosuggestions and AI/ML problems in the Search domain  Where conversational and agentic search changes how customers get to a decision. Making search work across three brands, multiple languages, and query behaviour that differs market by market. Our humble expectations We're looking for a product leader more than a feature owner. Someone who can find the problems that matter most, for customers and for the business, and make the case for solving them. You bring proven experience as a Product Manager in Consumer, or on another relevance- or ranking-driven consumer experience. You demonstrate fluency with search measurement and know how to actually move it. You show strong product judgment, backed by data literacy and customer insight. You work backwards from the customer problem, and you can weigh that against the most urgent business problems at the same time, rather than treating it as a side you have to pick. You think strategically: you can zoom out to where the domain should be in two years, then zoom back in on what we should ship next quarter. You're comfortable with ambiguity and genuinely flexible. This industry is changing fast, AI most of all, and the plan we write in January won't be the plan in June. You work deeply with ML and engineering on relevance and ranking, without needing to be an ML expert yourself. You're curious about what AI actually changes for customers, and you can tell real value from hype. You build a case and bring people with you: engineering, design, analytics, and local market teams across three brands and many markets. You do your best work with range: global platform thinking one week, a specific market's reality the next. Next steps The position will be filled as soon as we find the right person, so make sure to apply as soon as you realize you really, really want to join us! jobs.description: Mission Integral wurde im Oktober 2024 von Lukas Zörner und Anil Can Baykal gegründet und gehört zu den am schnellsten wachsenden Startups Deutschlands. Wir bauen die führende AI-native Plattform für Buchhaltung, Lohnabrechnung und Steuern für europäische KMU, beginnend mit Deutschland. Unterstützt werden wir von General Catalyst, Cherry Ventures, Puzzle Ventures und Unternehmer:innen aus ganz Europa. Wir sind aktuell etwas über 50 Leute und stellen in zwei sehr unterschiedlichen Märkten ein. Auf der einen Seite Steuerberater:innen, Bilanzbuchhalter:innen und Lohnbuchhalter:innen, die bundesweit gesucht sind und die man aus festen Anstellungen heraus gewinnt. Auf der anderen AI Engineers, Product Builder und GTM-Profile, um die in Berlin die stärksten Companies mitbieten. Als Talent Acquisition Manager:in übernimmst du einen Teil dieser Rollen und begleitest sie von Anfang bis Ende, vom Intake mit dem Team bis zur unterschriebenen Zusage. Du bist der erste Hire im Talent Team, entsprechend wenig ist bisher festgelegt und entsprechend viel kannst du selbst entscheiden. Deine Verantwortung Du verantwortest eigene Vakanzen über den kompletten Zyklus: Intake, Sourcing, Screening, Interview-Loop, Debrief, Angebot und Abschluss. Aktives Sourcing ist ein großer Teil der Rolle. Du identifizierst die Profile, die wir suchen, sprichst sie direkt an und überzeugst sie von einem Wechsel, über den sie vorher nicht nachgedacht haben. Recherche, Longlists und Ansprache gehören dir. Auf der Inbound-Seite verantwortest du die eingehenden Bewerbungen, von der Sichtung über die Erstgespräche bis zur Rückmeldung. Nach jeder Veröffentlichung kommt in den ersten Tagen das meiste Volumen, und wer schnell reagiert, führt die besten Gespräche zuerst. Du arbeitest eng mit den Hiring Managern zusammen: Anforderungsprofil gemeinsam schärfen, bevor die erste Sichtung läuft, Bewertungskriterien vorab festlegen, Debriefs moderieren. Wo ein Interview-Loop besser laufen kann, schlägst du Änderungen vor und setzt sie um Du legst fest, woran wir Recruiting messen. Du entscheidest mit, welche Zahlen wir brauchen, erhebst sie und reportest sie regelmäßig. Wenn eine Suche nicht läuft, sagst du früh Bescheid und kannst erklären, woran es liegt. jobs.title: Senior Product Manager (f/m/d)
jobs.description: About us Zenjob is an AI-powered flexible staffing platform that has connected companies and temporary workers since 2015. Companies use our platform to book ready-to-work staff in real time, while students use our app - we call them Zenjobbers - to find part-time jobs that conveniently fit around their studies. Over 40,000 Zenjobbers and 1,000 partner companies from logistics, retail, and hospitality in all major German cities share our belief that good work is not a coincidence. It is the result of innovative technology and genuine commitment. Good work starts here. The Role We are seeking a highly skilled Senior Product Manager to join our team. In this role, you will play a key part in defining and executing a product vision that ensures Zenjob’s marketplace dynamics are well balanced, by optimizing our demand forecast, making sure jobs and Zenjobbers are matched optimally, and engaging students in working a high number of shifts. This is not a role that owns one squad's backlog. You'll work project-based: form a team around a problem, own it end-to-end until it delivers on the expected need. You'll get problem statements, not requirements documents. Recent examples: how shifts get allocated across thousands of Zenjobbers each week, and how we get a new Zenjobber from signup to their first shift without human intervention. This role suits a Product Manager who is energised by an open-ended problem, and who finds complex workflows genuinely interesting. You'll report to the Director of Product and work across our Supply, Demand and Staffing squads, depending on the problem to solve. What You’ll do Bring our business goals to reality. Understand our financial goals, our users' problems and transform them into solutions that drive our revenue up. Talk to users directly . Zenjobbers, clients, and our own internal teams. Most of the good opportunities come out of these conversations, not out of a backlog. Do your own data work . You don’t wait until a data analyst gives you the insights, you dive into it and derive them yourself. Turn ambiguity into a defensible plan . Take a problem nobody agrees on yet, and define what we're solving, what we're explicitly not solving, and in what order. Design and run tests . Form a hypothesis, define what would falsify it, ship the smallest thing that gives you a real answer, and be honest about the result. Drive product development from concept to launch . Pull together Engineering, Design, Ops and Commercial around a problem and keep them moving through hypothesis, building, rollout and post-launch decision making Own the outcome, not the output . Each project has a number attached. You define what success looks like up front, and you're the one who says whether it was hit. Communicate clearly. A one-page memo an exec can act on. A spec an engineer doesn't have to interpret. A tradeoff explained to Commercial in terms they care about. What we’re looking for 6+ years in product, with meaningful time on products where the software coordinates real-world processes - staffing, logistics, fintech ops, healthcare, or similar, with substantial business impact. You have experience in marketplace dynamics and allocation problems. You've shipped something complex end-to-end and can talk credibly about what broke, not just what launched. You're analytically strong - comfortable getting to an answer yourself rather than commissioning one, and having a fluent conversation with data scientists. You've moved teams you don't manage . Cross-functional influence without formal authority is most of this job. You write and speak clearly. jobs.description: About Wolt At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we're building the delivery of (almost) everything and you'll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe. Working at Wolt isn't always easy, but it's definitely exciting. Here you'll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You'll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you're a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life. We're looking for a Product Manager to own our search experience that millions of customers land on when they open DoorDash, Wolt, or Deliveroo, and the single biggest lever we have on what they find. The role sits in our Core Consumer organisation in the Search domain, which is responsible for the in-app experience. You'll be building on a global stack, and your roadmap will be a mix: global platform problems that apply worldwide, global capabilities we're accelerating into EMEA markets, and EMEA-specific problems worth solving properly rather than working around. Search is where customers tell us exactly what they want. Getting it right across restaurants, grocery, and retail - in every language we operate in - is one of the highest-intent and hardest problems in the app. What you'll work on Query understanding, Autosuggestions and AI/ML problems in the Search domain  Where conversational and agentic search changes how customers get to a decision. Making search work across three brands, multiple languages, and query behaviour that differs market by market. Our humble expectations We're looking for a product leader more than a feature owner. Someone who can find the problems that matter most, for customers and for the business, and make the case for solving them. You bring proven experience as a Product Manager in Consumer, or on another relevance- or ranking-driven consumer experience. You demonstrate fluency with search measurement and know how to actually move it. You show strong product judgment, backed by data literacy and customer insight. You work backwards from the customer problem, and you can weigh that against the most urgent business problems at the same time, rather than treating it as a side you have to pick. You think strategically: you can zoom out to where the domain should be in two years, then zoom back in on what we should ship next quarter. You're comfortable with ambiguity and genuinely flexible. This industry is changing fast, AI most of all, and the plan we write in January won't be the plan in June. You work deeply with ML and engineering on relevance and ranking, without needing to be an ML expert yourself. You're curious about what AI actually changes for customers, and you can tell real value from hype. You build a case and bring people with you: engineering, design, analytics, and local market teams across three brands and many markets. You do your best work with range: global platform thinking one week, a specific market's reality the next. Next steps The position will be filled as soon as we find the right person, so make sure to apply as soon as you realize you really, really want to join us! jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.description: <p><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>At Too Good To Go, we dream of a planet with no food waste.</strong></span></p> <p>Did you know that more than 40% of all food produced gets thrown away? This unnecessary food waste — and the resources needed to produce and transport it — accounts for 10% of global greenhouse gas emissions.</p> <p>Too Good To Go is a certified B Corporation on a mission to end food waste. We connect stores with surplus food to consumers across 20 markets in Europe, North America, and APAC — with over 140 million registered users, more than 200,000 daily active stores, and 600 million meals saved from going to waste.</p> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>Why This Role</strong></span></p> <p>Pricing sits at the centre of everything we do. It shapes what partners earn, what consumers pay, and how much surplus food actually gets saved. Today, pricing decisions are made in different places, for different reasons, without a single team owning the strategy end to end.</p> <p>We are changing that. We are building our first dedicated Pricing team — and you will be the founding member.</p> <p>You will start with a concrete, high-value problem: the pricing infrastructure behind our Key Account deals. That's your launchpad — from there, you will have real scope to shape our approach to dynamic pricing, consumer-facing service fees, and pricing strategy across Too Good To Go more broadly. This is a role built for someone who wants to define a domain, not just execute a brief.</p> <p>The goal behind everything we do is twofold: save as much surplus food as possible, and grow the pie between TGTG, our Partners, and our Consumers — never trading one off against the other.</p> <p>There is a further dimension to this. We are expanding beyond food into new non-food, non-perishable categories — and that growth brings pricing complexity and opportunity we have not had to solve before. Getting ahead of that, rather than reacting to it, is part of this role.</p> <p><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>Your Mission</strong></span></p> <p>As Senior Product Manager for Pricing, you will build the foundation for how Too Good To Go prices its marketplace — starting with Key Account deals, then extending across the business.</p> <p>In the near term, you will design and ship the infrastructure that lets us set, manage, and evolve pricing for Key Account partnerships with the flexibility our commercial teams need. From there, you will develop a smarter, more dynamic pricing algorithm that responds to supply, demand, and partner economics — replacing static rules with something genuinely intelligent. Alongside this, you will investigate our consumer-facing service fees: how they're structured, how they're perceived, and where there is room to optimise.</p> <p>Underneath all of it are two questions you will own: how do we price in a way that saves as much surplus food as possible, and how do we grow the pie for everyone — Too Good To Go, our Partners, and our Consumers — rather than shifting value from one side to another? Answering both well means understanding marketplace pricing broadly: the best practices and patterns other two- and three-sided marketplaces use, and what applies to ours.</p> <p>Pricing decisions rarely stay inside one product's boundaries, so you will work across product teams and the wider organisation — Commercial, Data Science, Engineering, Finance, and Key Accounts — to make sure pricing is right everywhere it shows up, not just within your own roadmap. You will become the go-to person for anything pricing-related at Too Good To Go, including presenting your strategy and results to the Global Management Team.</p> <p&

jobs.description: <h3>About Dwelly</h3> <p>Dwelly is building the AI operating system for residential lettings. Its growing network of agencies provides its AI with real-world data, continuous feedback, and control over complete workflows, making exceptional service the standard for landlords and tenants. Today, Dwelly operates more than 15,000 properties and $470 million in GMV, making it one of the UK’s ten largest lettings operators. The company has raised $263 million.<br><br>We’re a fast-growing, product-focused company, backed by top-tier investors and led by a team with deep experience in real estate, technology, and operations.</p> <h3>Position Summary</h3> <p>We are seeking a highly talented and hands-on Product Designer to help shape the experience across the full set of Dwelly products (Tenant Find, Property Management, Payments, CRM) and the internal back-office tools that power them. This role involves deeply understanding our user personas (Tenant, Landlord, Maintenance Contractor, Dwelly Agent) and designing for both the customer-facing portals and the operational tools our agents use every day.</p> <p>Given the early stage of the business, our current products are hyper-functional but quite basic — an "MVP" that prioritises getting the job done across all domains. You'll work closely with product and engineering to take these to the next level: bringing clarity, usability, and craft to data-dense, workflow-heavy internal tools, and building genuinely good experiences for tenants and landlords. You'll also help establish the basic building blocks of design at Dwelly — a shared design system, patterns, and a lightweight design process — from the ground up.</p> <p>Our current development team is a team of 5, a few analysts, and one product designer. You'll join a small, fast-moving product team and have an outsized impact on how the whole product looks, feels, and works.</p> <h3><strong>Key Responsibilities:</strong></h3> <p><strong>1. </strong><strong>User Research &amp; Insights</strong></p> <ul> <li>Work with product to understand user pain points across all personas — tenants, landlords, maintenance contractors, and internal agents.</li> <li>Turn qualitative and quantitative insights into design decisions.</li> <li>Act as an advocate for usability and the end user within the company.</li> </ul> <p><strong>2. End-to-End Product Design</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design flows, wireframes, and high-fidelity UIs for both customer-facing products (tenant and landlord portals) and internal back-office tools.</li> <li>Design for data-dense, workflow-heavy operational products where clarity and efficiency matter more than decoration.</li> <li>Own the design process from concept and prototyping through to polished, build-ready specs, and iterate after launch.</li> </ul> <p><strong>3. jobs.description: SpAItial is pioneering Physically-grounded World Models, a new AI paradigm designed to generate and reason about the appearance and physics of real and imagined environments. We are moving beyond 2D pixels to build models that natively understand the geometry of our world, and redefining how industries from robotics and AR/VR to gaming and cinema create and interact with 3D environments. We are looking for our first Technical Artist to create attention around SpAItial. A technical artist and prototyper, with a public social presence built on your own films, stills, and demos. You sit next to our product engineers. You own the social presence that puts SpAItial in front of an audience, the artefacts that prove the models, and the prototypes that make the work felt. Key qualifications 3+ years of professional experience in technical art, VFX, real-time 3D, creative technology, or a similar role. A track record of building an audience. A portfolio of things you made yourself, publicly visible. We will spend more time on your films, stills, and prototypes than on your CV. Technical-artist craft on 3D content. A background in design, architecture, industrial design, animation, or VFX, or another discipline that trains you to think spatially and in shots. jobs.description: <div class="content-intro"><h3><strong>About Phaidra</strong></h3> <p>Phaidra is building the future of industrial automation.</p> <p>The world today is filled with static, monolithic infrastructure. Factories, power plants, buildings, etc. operate the same they've operated for decades — because the controls programming is hard-coded. Thousands of lines of rules and heuristics that define how the machines interact with each other. The result of all this hard-coding is that facilities are frozen in time, unable to adapt to their environment while their performance slowly degrades.</p> <p>Phaidra creates AI-powered control systems for the industrial sector, enabling industrial facilities to automatically learn and improve over time. Specifically:</p> <ul> <li>We use reinforcement learning algorithms to provide this intelligence, converting raw sensor data into high-value actions and decisions.</li> <li>We focus on&nbsp;industrial&nbsp;applications, which tend to be well-sensorized with measurable KPIs —&nbsp;perfect for reinforcement learning.</li> <li>We enable domain experts (our users) to&nbsp;configure&nbsp;the AI control&nbsp;systems (i.e. agents) without writing code. They define what they want their AI agents to do, and we do it for them.</li> </ul> <p>Our team has a track record of applying AI to some of the toughest problems. jobs.title: Data Analyst - Routing & Sortation
jobs.description: Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M), led by deep-tech investors Plural (whose portfolio spans fusion energy and space exploration), Relay is scaling faster than 99.98% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction . Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people , making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone. THE TEAM • ~110 people , more than half in engineering, product and data • 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research • Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle • An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking , tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation Overview Relay is a parcel delivery network. Every night, parcels from online retailers arrive at our sort centres, are sorted into delivery routes, and go out the next day with couriers. Two things have to go right for that to work. Routing is the planning side: software that decides, before parcels have even arrived, which ones to expect, how to group them into routes, and how to make those routes efficient for couriers to drive. Sortation is the physical side: warehouse teams and sorting robots turning a building full of parcels into neatly separated routes, thousands of times a night. The two are tightly coupled. If the plan expects a parcel that never arrives, a courier's route has a hole in it. If the warehouse sorts a parcel the plan didn't expect, it has nowhere to go. This role owns the analytics across both: spotting when either side is off, working out why, and building the case for what to change. Your work splits between a daily operational rhythm (is the network healthy this morning, and if not, why) and deeper investigations (what is driving cost, where is the plan falling short of what's possible, what should we change). Your analysis won't sit in a dashboard waiting to be discovered - it will change which parcels get planned for, how warehouse shifts are scheduled, and where the operation focuses its improvement efforts. Relay operates a centralised data team of around 30 data engineers, analysts, and data scientists, with analysts embedded into teams across the business. You will sit with the Routing & Sortation teams but report into the central data team, working daily with software engineers, warehouse operations, commercial, and finance. What You'll Do Routing Monitor the health of each night's route plans: how many parcels each route carries (planned vs what actually happened), how far couriers travel before their first delivery, and the routes no courier should ever be handed - a single parcel stranded miles from every other stop, or one route torn between two towns - and diagnose the cause when any of it moves Track how well we predict which parcels will arrive each night: when expected parcels don't show up, or unexpected ones do, work out whether the cause was the retailer's data, a warehouse error, or timing, and improve the prediction rules client by client Act on what you find: flag issues to warehouse managers and retailer-facing teams, and correct the plan when a retailer's parcels arrive outside the normal flow Monitor the route optimisation engine itself and flag regressions when the software or its inputs change Quantify how route design affects courier productivity: deliveries per hour, stops per route, distance between drops - and how far our actual routes sit from the best theoretically possible Build the reporting that diagnoses the middle leg of the network: the van journeys that move sorted parcels from sort centres ou

jobs.title: Senior Data Platform Engineer
jobs.description: We are looking for a  Senior Data Platform Engineer to join the Data Platform at Smartly! Smartly is building the standard path for governed data sharing across product services, analytics, and AI/ML. The Data Platform team owns the contracts, control mechanisms, publication paths, catalog metadata, lifecycle rules, lineage, permissions, and runtime building blocks that make reusable data safe and practical at scale. This is a role for someone who wants to shape a platform early, while working on concrete production problems from the start. Smartly already has the production systems, Kafka backbone, PostgreSQL databases, analytical consumers, and AI/ML use cases that need a better data foundation. The challenge is to turn that reality into a standard path that engineers actually want to use. Our first milestone is focused: centrally managed publishing tables in service-owned PostgreSQL databases, captured through Debezium CDC into Kafka, and registered in DataHub with ownership, lifecycle, lineage, and impact-analysis metadata. Longer-term, the platform expands toward self-service data products, governed materialisations, durable shared state, and reusable data across Smartly's operational and analytical systems. This is not a role where you only maintain an existing reporting pipeline. You will help design and build the platform path that other engineering teams use when they publish and consume shared data. What you will do Design and build platform services, tools, and workflows for contract-driven data publishing and consumption. Build the first production path for platform-managed PostgreSQL publishing tables, Debezium CDC, Kafka topics, and catalog registration. Create GitOps-style workflows where contracts, schemas, ownership, lifecycle, compatibility, policy metadata, and runtime desired state are reviewed, validated, and reconciled as code. Build tooling that gives product engineers fast feedback before they publish or change data products. Help define how Smartly models data products, publishing contracts, schema evolution, field stability, deletion semantics, access policy, lineage, and cost attribution. Operate and improve the CDC runtime model, including Kubernetes workloads, source-specific isolation, offsets, schema history, heartbeats, signal channels, lag visibility, replay, resnapshotting, and recovery. Integrate platform metadata into DataHub so engineers can discover data products, understand ownership, trace lineage, and reason about the impact of changes. Work with product, infrastructure, data engineering, analytics, and AI/ML teams to make the standard path easier and safer than bespoke point-to-point integrations. What we are looking for Strong experience building and operating production software systems, preferably in platform, infrastructure, backend, or data-intensive environments. Deep understanding of distributed systems trade-offs: reliability, idempotency, replay, eventual consistency, ownership boundaries, compatibility, and operational failure modes. Practical experience with PostgreSQL or other relational databases, including schema design, migrations, transactions, replication, or operational performance. Experience with Kafka, event streaming, CDC, Debezium, or adjacent data-movement technologies. Direct Debezium experience is valuable, but strong fundamentals matter more. jobs.description: <p>At JetBrains, code is our passion. Ever since we started, back in 2000, we have strived to make the strongest, most effective developer tools on earth. By automating routine checks and corrections, our tools speed up production, freeing developers to grow, discover, and create.</p> <p>The Business Application Development team builds and supports internal and customer-facing systems for licenses, subscriptions, billing, payments, reporting, and many other business-critical functions. Our domain is complex, our systems are interconnected, and there’s always a lot going on. We’re seeking a Senior Business Analyst to join the team and support our efforts.</p> <p>We’re not looking for someone who will just write requirements. We want someone who likes digging into problems, understanding how things actually work, talking to people, asking uncomfortable questions, and helping teams move toward practical and sustainable solutions.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll actually do:</strong></h2> <p>You’ll work closely with stakeholders, developers, and QA engineers, as well as sales, customer success, and other product teams, to figure out what problem we’re really solving, why it matters, what constraints exist, and what solution makes the most sense long term.</p> <p>A core responsibility is helping people stay focused on the actual goal instead of jumping straight to a “we need this exact feature” reaction. Though sometimes bigger, the right solution is often smaller than originally expected. The main job is frequently untangling the chaos and helping everyone align.</p> <p><strong>In this role, you will:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead discovery and requirements discussions.</li> <li>Organize and improve the intake and analysis process within the team.</li> <li>Structure requirements to support effective development.</li> <li>Help developers and QA engineers during implementation when new questions arise.</li> <li>Investigate unfamiliar areas independently rather than waiting for someone to explain.</li> <li>Think about edge cases, dependencies, risks, and long-term maintainability.</li> <li>Help reduce ambiguity around projects.</li> </ul> <p>We care deeply about balancing business value, implementation effort, technical limitations, and platform strategy. We’re not fans of overengineering, but we also don’t like quick hacks that create bigger problems down the line.</p> <h2><strong>We’ll be happy to bring you on board if you:</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Have solid experience in business analysis within software development teams.</li> <li>Understand how software development works end-to-end.</li> <li>Know how to structure complex information and turn messy discussions into clear requirements.</li> <li>Can stay focused on the core problem and avoid unnecessary complexity.</li> <li>Are comfortable discussing implementation details with engineers and understanding technical constraints.</li> <li>Can independently investigate unfamiliar functionality and connect dots across systems.</li> <li>Care about the overall result, not only your direct area of responsibility.</li> <li>Are proactive, curious, and comfortable working in an environment where not everything is perfectly documented.</li> <li>Can adapt your communication style and analytical approach depending on the people and context involved.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>It’d be a plus if you:</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Can work with SQL.</li> <li>Can read code well enough to understand what’s going on.</li> <li>Have experience with technically complex systems or system analysis.</li> &l

jobs.title: Senior Go Developer (f/m/d) – Focus on gRPC & Enterprise Applications
jobs.description: You'd build the Natuvion Cloud Portal, the Go/gRPC platform at the center of the company. It's the cloud counterpart to our core products and the central access point nearly every team works through, used by our own people and our customers alike. A year old, already the strategic core, mostly greenfield, and growing fast. What to expect The work is varied, and the problems rarely repeat. One stretch you might be making multi-tenant queries fly across 100 GiB+ tables in DuckDB; the next, packing a couple dozen services into a single binary a customer can run on-prem, or building our AI firewall, deep-packet inspection for AI traffic that decides, per customer and per user, exactly which AI tools and MCP servers are allowed. It's the kind of fine-grained control that enterprises with sensitive data actually need and almost nobody has built. The stack is deliberately solid, though we'll reach for newer tools where the benefit is substantial. Go and gRPC throughout, with Google's AIPs as a strict ruleset so our APIs stay compatible as the platform grows. We run on AWS/EKS and on-prem with no vendor lock-in, backed by PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, Redis, OpenSearch and a Grafana/Loki/Mimir/Jaeger stack, all shipped through GitHub Actions. Authorization is one such case: the platform's entire authz system is built on SpiceDB/Zanzibar, newer and less battle-tested, but exactly the right tool for the job. There's a dedicated SRE team, but you build it, you run it. You'd join four backend engineers, a flat team with a hands-on technical lead, and we're hiring across backend and frontend to keep up. Your Responsibilities : Design and build the gRPC services at the heart of the Cloud Portal, APIs that other teams depend on and that must stay compatible as the platform grows Take services end to end: design, ship, and run them in production, across both cloud and on-prem Solve the performance and scaling problems that come with multi-tenant systems and large datasets Help shape architecture and technical direction, where your input genuinely moves things in a team this small 5+ years writing production-grade Go Strong grasp of idiomatic Go, concurrency patterns, and profiling with pprof, plus a real understanding of escape analysis, allocation behavior, and what the GC is actually doing Solid experience building and maintaining APIs using gRPC, including Protobuf versioning, streaming, and API lifecycle best practices (bonus: you know Google AIPs) Proven experience with relational databases (PostgreSQL), performance tuning, and schema design Comfortable in cloud-native environments, applying caching, queuing, and observability best practices Professional working proficiency in English, enough to communicate complex technical ideas clearly to peers and stakeholders If you think that you don't meet all the requirements: With us, there are "no limits" to your development! Go your way with us - we support you! Just show us who you are. What you can expect from us: An environment that is always open to change and optimization. There is no "it's always been like this" with us. You have the opportunity to contribute your knowledge, design processes, standardize existing topics or optimize workflows. jobs.title: Working Student IT Operations (m/f/d)

We offer the world’s finest coffee and equipment to over 150,000 customers online and in our Cafés, driven by our goal to make high-end coffee experiences enjoyable and accessible to all. With over 5 million euros raised in donations, we cannot wait to increase our positive impact with you on our team, one cup of coffee at a time. Keep our UniFi networks and internet connections running and help troubleshoot issues remotely or on-site. Maintain and provision devices, keep our hardware inventory clean, and support onboarding and offboarding. Document setups, fixes, and processes in Notion so knowledge stays accessible. Support practical GDPR and information security topics, including TOMs, deletion concepts, access management, and security documentation. Report to our CTO and be part of our Tech Team. Your profile You’re currently enrolled at university, ideally in Computer Science, Business Informatics, or a related field. You have a basic understanding of networks and Linux and enjoy learning new technical topics. You work independently, stay organized, and appreciate good documentation. We do that through limited editions: co-branded drops with entertainment IPs, licensing deals with cultural icons, collaborations that make people genuinely excited about what they are eating. Are you a senior brand partnerships and licensing professional who closes deals, owns projects end-to-end, and has the network to make things happen from day one? If so, read on. YOUR TASKS Partner Identification & Pipeline Management: You proactively source, evaluate, and pitch licensing and co-branding opportunities across entertainment IPs, cultural icons, celebrities, and lifestyle brands. Deal Negotiation & Contracting: You lead negotiations end-to-end and close with confidence. LOIs, licensing agreements, talent contracts, commercial terms, royalties, usage rights. Concept, LOI, product development, packaging redesign, legal sign-off, market launch. You keep cross-functional teams across brand, product, design, legal, sales, retail, and D2C moving in the same direction and on time. Business Case & Performance Ownership: You build and own the business case for every collaboration: budget, margin, revenue forecast, and post-launch review. You track revenue contribution, retail sell-through, D2C performance, and brand awareness lift per edition, and use it to make the next one better. Internal Alignment & Launch Enablement: You brief and align brand, social, ecom, and retail on launch strategy, content needs, and sell-in materials so every edition lands the way it should, in-store and online. YOUR PROFILE You bring 5+ years in licensing, brand partnerships, or co-branding, ideally within FMCG, consumer lifestyle, entertainment, or a licensing/talent agency. You have negotiated and signed LOIs, licensing agreements, and talent contracts with full commercial responsibility. You come with a network of IP holders, agencies, talent managers, and entertainment companies that opens doors from day one. You are comfortable juggling multiple complex workstreams at once, aligning cross-functional teams without formal authority, and holding a timeline without micromanaging. You have owned 6-7 figure budgets and built business cases from zero. You communicate with confidence in both German and English. Native-level German and full fluency in English are required. You take responsibility for your projects and your numbers, make clear decisions even when the path is not, and thrive where speed and ownership matter. jobs.title: Technical Product Owner (m/f/d)
jobs.description: About us Since 2000, ITA Logistics Group has been making shipping simpler, more transparent, and more efficient for businesses. With our platforms LetMeShip and ParcelParcel , companies can quickly compare and directly book their daily shipping needs. By bringing together a wide range of carriers on our platforms, we combine modern technology with personal service. Across several locations in Europe, our teams work every day to simplify shipping processes in a sustainable way. We believe in open collaboration and fast decision-making. That’s why we are looking for people who take ownership, contribute ideas, and want to actively shape the future with us. Your mission As our (Technical) Product Owner (m/f/d) , you will be part of our Product Team and take ownership of key technical interfaces and integrations across our platforms. Your main focus will be on our Customer APIs , the Unified Carrier Interface (UCI) , and, going forward, the Unified Financial Platform (UFP) as well as our HubSpot integration . You will work at the intersection of Product, Engineering, and Business. You understand technical dependencies, translate different requirements into clear priorities, and work closely with our teams to ensure that our integrations are reliable and continuously evolving. You will collaborate closely with our Product Owners, Technical Business Analyst, Software Engineers, and Data Insights team while also acting as an important point of contact for internal stakeholders, customers, carriers, and external partners. Your Key Responsibilities You own and continuously develop the roadmap for our Customer APIs across LMS Enterprise and LMS Next. You drive the migration of our API customers from LMS Enterprise to LMS Next , identifying and prioritizing the features and carrier integrations required to make the transition successful. You act as a technical point of contact for our API customers, supporting them with questions, troubleshooting, and technical challenges. You take ownership of the development of our Unified Carrier Interface (UCI) in close collaboration with internal and external stakeholders. You analyze requirements for carrier features and services, translate them into clear requirements for Engineering, and support QA in defining relevant test cases. You communicate directly with our carriers to clarify technical requirements and integration specifics. Once live, you take ownership of our Unified Financial Platform (UFP) and manage its backlog, requirements, and further development. You continuously monitor our existing HubSpot integration and prioritize adjustments based on evolving business needs and feedback. Across all these areas, you connect Engineering, business stakeholders, carriers, and external partners, ensuring clear requirements, priorities, and decisions. What you need to succeed You have a technical background , for example in Software Engineering or Computer Science, or several years of experience working at the intersection of Product and Engineering. You have experience as a Product Owner or Product Manager , ideally working with APIs, platforms, or technical integrations. You have a solid understanding of APIs, API design, versioning, and migration strategies and feel confident engaging in detailed technical discussions with engineers. You are able to understand complex technical topics and translate them clearly for different audiences. You are confident in stakeholder management and know how to balance and prioritize competing technical and business needs. You are comfortable managing multiple workstreams and adapting to changing priorities while keeping a clear overview of what matters most. You enjoy working collaboratively across teams and locations, including with colleagues in Hamburg and Naarden . You are curious about AI tools and digital solutions and enjoy exploring new ways to improve productivity, processes, and workflows. Experience in logistics, parcel, or freight tech , particular

jobs.title: Lead Java Developer/Solution Architect (6-month contract)
jobs.description: gravity9 is recruiting Java engineers and architects for a portfolio of engagements across UK central government. These are large-scale, data-intensive modernisation programmes: replacing legacy systems that carry statutory weight, decomposing monoliths that serve millions of users, and building secure data platforms where access control and auditability are first-class architectural concerns rather than late additions. We are hiring across two overlapping profiles — Senior Java Developer and Application / Migration Architect — and expect most people to move between programmes as engagements start and complete. Several of these are hands-on architect roles: you will own design decisions and also write production code The kind of work The following are representative of current and upcoming engagements. Individual roles will draw on some of this, not all of it — we are more interested in engineers who can work confidently at the intersection of Java and data than in a checklist match against any one programme. Secure data catalogue and access-control platform A greenfield metadata catalogue acting as a federated index over data held across independent domains, so that authorised parties can locate and retrieve data the catalogue itself never holds. The work includes designing an attribute-based access control model over attributes such as clearance, nationality, organisational unit and compartment; enforcing those policies inside the database query path rather than filtering results afterwards; application-layer encryption with externally managed keys; hybrid lexical and semantic search with access filtering applied before candidate retrieval rather than after it; and a tamper-evident audit trail that can reconstruct why a given record was returned, redacted or withheld. Real-time decision-support data architecture Replacing point-to-point integration across a multi-vendor estate with a microservices architecture and a common data layer, so that operational data flows in near real time instead of over days. The work includes target-state architecture and decision records, change-data-capture ingest pipelines from upstream data services, ontology and mapping-layer design across suppliers with competing data models, separation of system, reference and insight data classes including time-series, and deployment topologies spanning cloud-hosted services down to constrained edge hardware. Legacy-to-document-model migration at national scale Migrating hundreds of millions of records and tens of terabytes of XML out of a legacy relational platform into a sharded document store, in support of a COBOL-to-Java microservices rewrite. The work includes a configuration-driven XML-to-JSON transformation framework backed by a versioned schema registry — twenty years of history, multiple record types and continual schema and semantic drift; CDC and streaming pipelines, or a checkpointed parallel bulk-extract alternative; a field-level mapping validation and reconciliation framework robust enough to stand up to audit; a replay and failure-diagnostics harness with dead-letter routing and idempotent re-runs; and repeated dress rehearsals toward a single cutover window with no dual running. Monolith decomposition and data-ownership migration Breaking a distributed monolith of well over a hundred Java services sharing a handful of database clusters into domain-owned services — moving from borrowed data to owned data without reintroducing hidden coupling. The work includes bounded-context analysis to establish which domain genuinely owns which collections, in-place data remodelling ahead of any physical move, a data-access facade with feature-flagged per-request routing between old and new stores, dual-write / backfill / reconcile / read-switch cutover lifecycles with a defined rollback at every step, cluster-to-cluster streaming and live migration tooling, and automated parallel-run and diff-on-read testing. Demonstrated experience using AI and/or coding automation to get controls built, implemented, and operating in practice. jobs.title: New Patient Nurse
jobs.description: If you became a nurse because you wanted to genuinely make a difference to patients lives, but you are ready to do it in a completely different way, this could be the role for you. We are looking for experienced nurses who are ready to step away from traditional ways of working and into an innovative, fully remote clinical environment. You will speak to patients who have often spent years trying different treatments and managing conditions that have had a huge impact on their everyday lives. This is a different way of nursing. You will use your clinical experience, judgement and ability to really listen to patients to help decide the next step in their treatment journey. It is fast paced, constantly evolving and you will need to be comfortable with change. Most importantly, you will be working somewhere where the patient genuinely is at the centre of what we do and where the decisions you make can have a real impact on someone's quality of life. What is the Role? This is a remote clinical role sitting at the heart of the patient journey at Montu. As a New Patient Nurse, you will be the first clinical point of contact for patients seeking cannabis-based medical treatment. You will conduct structured video consultations to gather medical histories, assess suitability, and determine whether a patient is ready to progress to one of our consultants. This role does not include prescribing or treatment delivery. What it does include is complex clinical decision-making, a fast-moving caseload, and patients who have often tried everything else before reaching us. You will need to be confident working autonomously, comfortable in a fully remote environment, and genuinely invested in getting the right outcome for every patient. If you are looking for a quiet life, this is not the role for you. If you want to do meaningful clinical work from home and be part of a growing team that is changing how patients access medicine, it is. This is a full-time role, working 40 hours per week. You will be required to work 1 Saturday per month, for which a day in lieu will be provided. This role is fully remote. What Will You Be Doing? Conducting video-based pre-assessment consultations with prospective patients Taking detailed medical histories including current medications, relevant family history, and prior treatment Assessing patient suitability for referral to Montu's clinical consultants Maintaining accurate, confidential patient records Guiding patients clearly through the onboarding process and answering clinical questions appropriately Escalating safeguarding concerns and contraindications in line with Montu policy and national guidance What You Need Essential NMC-registered Nurse with a minimum of 5 years post-registration clinical experience UK-based nursing degree or equivalent qualification Previous experience working as a nurse in a remote clinical environment, including conducting patient consultations via telephone or video Confident autonomous decision-maker with strong clinical reasoning Clear and effective communicator, both written and verbal Comfortable working in a fully remote, tech-enabled environment including video platforms and EMRs Sound understanding of safeguarding, GDPR, and clinical governance Desirable Background in pain management, cannabis-based medicinal products, or complementary therapies Experience in a fast-paced or high-volume clinical setting What We Offer Generous Leave: 25 days holiday (rising to 27 after year one and 30 after year three) + 8 bank holidays Pension Matching: Up to 5% employer matching contributions Private Healthcare Scheme Flexibility and Wellness: Work-from-home options, cycle-to-work scheme, and more Growth Opportunities: Collaborate across teams and represent Montu at events, with support to grow your skills and impact Enhanced Maternity & Paternity Leave About Us Montu UK is a leading digital health company specialising in cannabis-based medicines (CBPM), dedicated to improving patien

jobs.title: Consultant Psychiatrist PAYE
jobs.description: An opportunity to help patients who have run out of options For many people living with chronic pain, the journey has been long. They have tried multiple medications, procedures and therapies, yet their pain continues to impact every aspect of daily life. By the time they reach us, many are looking for another option where conventional treatment has fallen short. We are Montu UK, one of the UK's largest medical cannabis clinics, and we are looking for Consultants specialising in Pain Management to join our clinical team. About the role You will assess and manage patients exploring cannabis based medicines, making the clinical decision on whether treatment is appropriate and managing their care from there. This is an evolving area of medicine where the evidence base continues to grow, giving you the opportunity to help shape how cannabis based medicines are used within pain management in the UK. You do not need previous experience with cannabis based medicines. We are looking for experienced Pain Management Consultants with sound clinical judgement, an open mind and a genuine interest in improving outcomes for patients with complex chronic pain. We provide comprehensive specialist training, and our multidisciplinary model means you are never working in isolation. Nurses and pharmacists complete pre consultation and follow up prescribing tasks, allowing you to focus on clinical decision making and patient care. What you will be doing: Provide high quality care for patients seeking medical cannabis treatment. Conduct patient consultations, including assessment and ongoing management. Engage in clinical outcome data collection to support evidence based practices. Contribute to clinical governance and maintain robust patient care standards. Collaborate effectively within a multidisciplinary team, including nurses and pharmacists. Participate in ongoing training and professional development, including bespoke specialist training in cannabis based medicines (CBMPs). What you need: Full GMC Registration Completion of Specialist Training (CCST/CCT) or equivalent certification On the GMC Specialist Register for Pain Demonstrated interest in alternative therapies Willingness to participate in data collection and reporting Why join us? Highly Competitive Salary: £190,000 - £275,000 FTE, pro rata for part time roles based on experience and hours worked. Flexible Working: Full time or part time options available Comprehensive Indemnity Coverage: Montu will cover all professional and clinical indemnity insurance for your work with us Private Healthcare Work-Life Balance: No night shifts or on call requirements Cutting Edge Training: Access to CPD accredited medical cannabis education and specialist in house training from industry leaders Collaborative Environment: Join a multidisciplinary team of healthcare professionals Personal Growth: Be part of a pioneering field and shape the future of medical cannabis care in the UK Training & Development: Attendance at a recognised Medical Cannabis Course for Specialist Physicians (sponsored by Montu) Specialist training delivered by experts, including Prof Anup Mathew (Consultant Psychiatrist) and Dr Gerard Sinovich (Pain Management Consultant). Ongoing support and training on clinical protocols, prescribing practices, and Montu’s system usage Working arrangements: Remote Role: Flexible working hours and days Session Structure: Standard session length: 4 hours Appointment duration: 15 minutes (new and existing patients) Montu’s multidisciplinary model allows consultants to focus on prescribing and patient care, while nurses and pharmacists handle pre consultation and follow up tasks. If you are passionate about innovative patient care, thrive in a dynamic environment, and are looking to make a real impact in the field of medical cannabis, we would love to hear from you! Sessions: Each standard session consists of 4 hours of patient consultations. Clinicians can choose their preferred working days

jobs.title: Growth Creative Operations
jobs.description: TL;DR: Lovable's growth marketing runs on creative. The volume, variety, and quality of concepts we put in front of people, and how fast what we learn from them turns into the next round. Your job is to own that loop end to end, constantly iterating on it to achieve the best results against your KPIs. Why Lovable? Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started. We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world. Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software. What we’re looking for You've run high-volume creative testing on performance marketing and can talk specifically about what you learned, not just what you shipped. You use AI tools daily and have built something with them that other people now depend on. A workflow, an agent, an internal tool, a tagging pipeline. You have opinions about what makes an ad work and can articulate them well. You write well for ads. Briefs, hooks, scripts etc. You're comfortable being wrong in public. A lot of tests lose, and the loop only works if we’re all comfortable with that. You move fast, but balance that with exceptional craft and know where the balance is. What you’ll do You'll be the person who decides what we test, why, and what the results mean. Then you'll build the workflows that turn those answers into hundreds of assets a month without losing the taste that made them work in the first place. Own the creative operating system. You run creative ops for performance marketing: intake, briefing, production, QA, launch, and post-mortem. You'll define how the process works and then automate the parts that don't need a human in the loop. Be the creative performance decision maker. When we can produce hundreds of creatives, you’ll be the person to judge what we make more of, what gets killed and what to slightly edit. That means holding the creative standard high, and making sure that creatives generated look Lovable. Build agentic workflows and keep improving them. You'll design pipelines that generate, adapt, and localise creative at volume, with evals to check quality before anything ships. When a workflow breaks, you diagnose it and help rebuild it. Turn performance data, audience insights and product knowledge into concepts. You'll dig into what's actually driving results, hook, format, message, subject, pacing, offer, and separate the signal from the noise a low-spend winner creates. Run brainstorms and briefing. You own the rhythm that takes learnings, customer language, competitor moves, product releases, and additional context, and works with the wider team to turn them into briefs. Push learnings across the company. What wins on paid usually tells us something about the website, lifecycle emails, App Store listings, and organic content. You'll be the one making sure that reaches the relevant people so we become more informed collectively. About your application Please submit your application in English. It’s our company language, so you’ll be speaking lots of i

jobs.title: New Grad Software Engineer
jobs.description: New Grad Software Engineer (2026 or 2027) We’re a profitable video game start-up in London with 15 million monthly players and we’re hiring New Grad Software Engineers (2026 or 2027) to join our 11-person founding team. About us Creating games with editable worlds usually takes 20k+ lines of well-optimised code and large amounts of effort. Bloxd gives you editable worlds in 5 lines of code, within 5 minutes. You can play our games at bloxd.io . About you You’re equally excited by difficult engineering problems as you are by voxel, sandbox, and multiplayer games. You think deeply about what makes these games fun and enjoy building the technical systems that make them possible. You have robust engineering fundamentals, a high-ownership mentality and enjoy working collaboratively. You are eager to wear many hats across game design, UI/UX, and community management, and can iterate quickly on a live product whilst learning from player feedback. What we’re looking for A degree in computer science, engineering, mathematics, or a related subject, or equivalent practical experience. Some professional experience in software engineering, either through internships, or scaled side projects. Experience developing games, game engines or modding through side projects. Things you could work on within your first 2 months: Create and manage your own game Develop new gameplay systems inside existing games Build new engine features for use by other game developers Profile and optimise performance Develop an in-game item marketplace Improve our partner implementations (E.g. CrazyGames, Discord Activities) Play a lot of Bloxd :) Our tech We have a TypeScript-first codebase, and use a combination of React, WebGL, and Node. This tech allows us to deliver Bloxd in an incredibly accessible way, and provides a great developer experience. You’ll need to be happy to pick these up if you’re not already familiar with them. Benefits Healthcare 5% pension match on qualifying earnings A permanent desk in our King’s Cross office 25 days holiday + bank holidays Competitive salary + stock options Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

jobs.title: Cross Sales Specialist
jobs.description: Join us as a Cross Sales Specialist Want to do work that really matters? At Checkatrade, we’re building the UK’s go-to home improvement marketplace. Every day, we help millions of homeowners find the right tradesperson for the job, fast, fair, and without the faff. As our next Cross Sales Specialist , you’ll help us grow that impact. By connecting with trades and showing the value of joining Checkatrade, you’ll help build stronger businesses and stronger homes across the UK. Forget long lists, here’s what you’ll actually spend your time on: Engaging potential customers and converting leads into Checkatrade members. Using solution-based selling to show how we support trade businesses to grow. Handling objections with confidence and closing with clarity. Keeping Salesforce data tidy, accurate and up to date. Working with other teams to share insight, learn fast, and keep smashing targets. It’s not about ticking every box. It’s about turning up curious, ready to crack on. You’ll do well here if you bring: Proven experience in a sales role, with a strong track record of hitting targets. A confident communicator who’s not afraid to pick up the phone and make things happen. Resilience, drive, and a hunger to exceed expectations. Solid objection-handling and negotiation skills. A proactive, self-motivated mindset and a knack for spotting opportunities. Experience using Salesforce or a similar CRM to manage your pipeline. We believe great work deserves great rewards. Here’s just a taste: Competitive salary + uncapped commission structure Health, well-being and learning support Gym membership, Smart Tech Scheme and Cycle Scheme Birthday/Special day leave Buy & sell holiday scheme 1 week’s paid charity leave and much more! How we’ll get to know each other: Screening call with one of our Talent Acquisition Partners 1st stage interview with our Associate Manager, Cross Sales & Head of Cross Sales 2nd stage interview with VP of Sales If you require any reasonable adjustments during our interview process, please discuss them with your Talent Acquisition Partner. If this sounds like the place you’ll thrive, we’d love to hear from you, even if you don’t tick every single box. About us We’re Checkatrade – the UK’s leading platform for finding a tradesperson. With more than 50,000 trades listed and over 6 million reviews, we help homeowners get jobs done right and help tradespeople grow their business. We’re growing fast, with big plans to become the go-to brand for home improvements. If you care about great work, take pride in the details, and want to make an impact, you’ll fit right in. jobs.title: Revenue Operations Manager
jobs.description: Revenue Operations Manager 📍 Manchester, UK (Hybrid 2 days WFH) | 💰 Up to £70,000 Street Group is one of the fastest-growing PropTech companies in the UK. We want to be the leading creator of delightful experiences for everybody involved in buying, selling, renting and letting property, regardless of their involvement, to improve the industry for everyone by elevating UK estate agencies through world-class technology. Your job is to own the numbers for the entire commercial engine. Not hit them, own them. You'll build the single version of the truth that runs our marketing, sales and customer success functions, and put a reliable set of numbers in front of our leadership team and board. You will take accountability for the integrity of the full commercial funnel from top-of-funnel marketing through to churn and renewals. Right now, each function applies its own definitions and rules. You'll set one consistent set of rules and make them stick across the entire business. You'll also be responsible for forecasting, headcount planning and supporting the design of commission structures. This is a hands-on, senior operator role. You'll own the tech stack (HubSpot sits at the centre), and you'll build the workflows, automations and permissions that keep data clean at source. You're not tidying records by hand; you're designing systems. You'll also be working with AI daily – it's not optional here. We use Claude, and you'll need to show evidence of AI already embedded in how you work. There are no commissions or bonuses in this role and that is deliberate. The role has to stay objective about what the figures say. We've positioned the salary to reflect both your seniority and the independence you'll need to challenge senior leaders professionally and diplomatically when the numbers don't match the narrative. HERE'S WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT TO BE WORKING ON Building and maintaining complete visibility across the entire revenue line: marketing pipeline, sales pipeline, churn and renewals, and capacity planning. Setting and enforcing a single set of definitions and rules across marketing, sales and customer success, then making them stick. Owning HubSpot end-to-end: permissions, day-to-day usage, workflow build, automations and the processes that keep data clean at source. Producing forecasts, headcount plans and reporting that the leadership team can actually rely on. Contributing to the design of commission plans and commercial structures. Supporting the hiring and onboarding of a Sales Operations person, and training them to maintain what you've built. Presenting to the board, with numbers that are clean, consistent and defensible. Using AI to solve problems that would otherwise drown you in manual work. Joining up the revenue line with the wider business (think product, finance, and marketing) so everybody's working from the same playbook. WHY YOU SHOULD (AND SHOULDN'T) APPLY YOU SHOULD APPLY IF: You've owned reporting across a full commercial funnel (not just the sales pipeline). You can point to a forecast you owned, a commission plan you shaped and workflows you built yourself. HubSpot is second nature to you. You operate at expert or power-user level and you can configure permissions, automations and processes without breaking into a sweat. You've worked in multi-product SaaS at a senior level and you understand how different product lines affect pipeline, ARR and churn. AI is already woven into how you work. You can give concrete examples of which tools you use, what you've built with them, and how they've changed your process significantly. You can challenge senior leaders diplomatically but firmly, and you're not afraid to report the numbers as they actually are, not as people hope they'll be. You work best with autonomy. You're a self-starter who gets the work done yourself, not someone who needs to manage others to feel productive. We want to be the leading creator of delightful experiences for everyone buying, selling, renting and letting property, improving the industry for all of them by elevating UK estate agencies through world-class technology. If you join us, you'll be helping to improve the property industry for everyone by widening the reach of our products and introducing them to estate agents across the UK, in turn making agents more successful and helping them deliver an incredible customer experience. Proactively sourcing and nurturing leads to grow your pipeline and secure new business opportunities. Ensuring a seamless handover to, and close collaboration with, our Customer Success team, to increase client ROI and reduce churn. Sharing best practice and innovative approaches to B2B sales to enhance the effectiveness of the sales team. Working closely with our development teams to provide fresh ideas on product development. Ensuring our customers have a best-in-class experience at every opportunity. You consistently achieve and exceed sales targets through proactive prospecting and closing of deals. You bring energy and enthusiasm to your work, helping to create a positive and motivating atmosphere during outbound sessions. You keep your effort and activity levels high, contributing to a strong team dynamic through your actions and your example. You share ideas and approaches that improve the team's effectiveness and help refine our sales practices as we grow. You bring reliability and professionalism to all your interactions and responsibilities. Above all, you're goal-orientated and driven by exceeding targets. We're an award-winning PropTech business based in Manchester, founded in 2015 by brother-and-sister duo Tom and Heather Staff. Our products, Street.co.uk and Spectre, work harmoniously together to transform an agent's job. From securing more leads and winning new instructions to streamlining business operations and growing market share, our products are supercharging thousands of agencies across the UK. jobs.title: Associate Relationship Manager - London
jobs.description: About Allica Bank Allica is the UK’s fastest growing company - and the fastest-growing financial technology (Fintech) firm ever. Our purpose is to help established SMEs, one of the last major underserved opportunities in Fintech. Established SMEs are the backbone of local communities - representing over a third of our economy - yet have been largely neglected both by traditional high street banks and modern fintech providers. Department Description Our vision is to reimagine Relationship Banking for established SMEs, through the very best people, products and digital tools. Allica’s Relationship Management team was formed in 2022 and continues to grow at pace, providing established SME customers with expert human relationships alongside modern banking technology. The team supports customers with lending, current accounts, savings, asset finance and working capital facilities, while building deep local relationships with SME customers, trusted professional advisers and business communities. The Associate Relationship Manager role is a newly created position that is a key step in our ambition to build the best Relationship team to support our SME clients. The successful candidate will manage a portfolio of clients and be expected to deliver across a range of commercial, customer service and risk objectives whilst also providing support to the wider relationship team as part of their development. This is a great opportunity for someone looking to develop their skills and progress a career as an SME Relationship Manager. Principal Accountabilities Manage a portfolio of SME customers delivering outstanding customer service, building genuine and trusting relationships and develop a deep understanding of your clients’ businesses and their ambitions. Deliver against a range of commercial targets including lending and new customer / deposit acquisition, as well as identifying and meeting a range of client needs through the provision of Allica products and services. Build a trusted external network with SME advisers and the wider business community. Leverage this network to generate new business opportunities for the bank, in addition to signposting your clients to external support and advice as appropriate. Ensure that Risk is managed effectively on your portfolio, with all required risk activities completed on time and to a high standard. Use customer data and internal Allica systems to identify signs of client stress and take proactive action to tackle early. Work closely with a Senior Relationship Manager, contributing to building a bespoke personal development plan which will include supporting them and the wider team as part of your learning. Take an active role in new business campaigns, including attending events, following up on leads, supporting prospect engagement and undertaking some cold calling where appropriate. Support event organisation and follow-up activity, helping the team build strong local relationships with SME customers, prospects, accountants, solicitors and other trusted professional advisers. Maintain accurate CRM records, strong follow-up discipline and good control over customer, prospect and portfolio activity. Build strong, collaborative and productive relationships with your team and wider internal stakeholders to ensure customer needs are meet efficiently and any issues resolved quickly. Personal Attributes & Experience Some B2B sales, account management and/or SME banking experience, with a clear interest in building a career in SME relationship banking and a passion for supporting SMEs to be more successful. Some experience of commercial lending and understanding / analysing financial accounts would be of benefit. Curious, proactive and keen to learn, with the motivation to develop lending, sales, risk management and portfolio management capability through formal training and on-the-job coaching. jobs.title: Data Scientist - Audiobooks Analytics
jobs.description: We are looking for a Data Scientist to join the Business Analytics team within Spotify’s Business Strategy and Insights organization. You will work with the Audiobooks Analytics Lead to help shape our global audiobooks strategy and improve the experience for listeners, creators, publishers, and authors. In this role, you will use data analysis, experimentation, and statistical modeling to evaluate some of the most important opportunities facing our audiobooks business. Your work will span content and catalog strategy, discovery and recommendations, subscriber growth, and new product and commercial initiatives. You will turn complex questions into clear recommendations and help senior leaders make confident decisions. You will collaborate with a distributed team of analysts, data scientists, business leaders, product managers, editorial partners, and engineers. At Spotify, you will have access to rich datasets and the autonomy to explore them creatively and rigorously. Above all, your work will help shape how the world listens to and discovers audiobooks. What You'll Do Develop data-driven strategies for audiobook catalog, content discovery, listener engagement, and subscriber growth. Evaluate new product, content, licensing, and commercial opportunities through forecasting, scenario modeling, and impact measurement. Partner with Editorial, Personalization, Product, Finance, and Business teams to improve title selection, recommendation quality, and the listener experience. Design and analyze experiments, including A/B tests and quasi-experiments, to measure the impact of product and go-to-market initiatives. Monitor the health of the audiobooks business, identify emerging opportunities or risks, and translate them into clear recommendations. Develop reliable analytical datasets, tools, and reporting that make important insights accessible and repeatable. Work with analytics engineering and data partners to improve data quality and create scalable ways of working. Present findings and recommendations to senior leaders, influencing the direction of our product and business. Who You Are You have 3+ years of professional experience in data science or analytics, ideally in consumer technology, media, subscriptions, marketplaces, or a similarly complex business. You are fluent in SQL and proficient in Python, R, or another programming language, with a strong grasp of statistical methods, experimentation, and causal inference. You combine analytical rigor with strong business judgment and can cleanly extract the “so what” from complex analysis. You are comfortable working through ambiguous problems, structuring open-ended questions, and identifying a practical path forward. You enjoy collaborating with a wide range of cross-functional partners and can build trust across technical and non-technical teams. You are an excellent communicator who can present complex findings clearly to senior leaders and audiences with different levels of technical knowledge. You have a degree in Economics, Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience. Experience with product analytics, recommendation systems, content businesses, or digital marketplaces is a plus. Where You'll Be This role is based in London. We offer flexibility to work where you work best. There will be some in-person meetings, while still allowing flexibility to work from home. Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listen
